subject: mathematics
question_text: If the A.M. and the G.M. between two numbers are in the ratio m : n, prove that the numbers are in the ratio m + √(m² − n²) : m − √(m² − n²).

mark_split.label: Write the ratio and apply componendo and dividendo
Apply the rule again and square

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name the rule you use twice and say what appears under the square root.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the ratio and apply componendo and dividendo
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both the ratio (a + b)/(2√(ab)) = m/n and the named rule must be written before the square root is taken.
steps.memory_tip: a + b ± 2√(ab) = (√a ± √b)², which is why componendo and dividendo is used here.
lines: Let the two numbers be a and b.

recall.must_convey: That (a + b)/(2√(ab)) = m/n, and componendo and dividendo gives (√a + √b)/(√a − √b) = √(m + n)/√(m − n).
accept: a m by g m is a plus b over two root a b
apply componendo and dividendo to get perfect squares
take the square root of both sides after the rule
componendo dividendo tho perfect square vasthundi
the ratio becomes m plus n over m minus n

steps.why: Adding and subtracting 2√(ab) turns both sides of the ratio into perfect squares, so the square root can be taken cleanly.
common_mistakes: Writing (a + b)/√(ab) = m/n and losing the 2 in the denominator.
Taking the square root of only one side of the ratio.

steps.label: Apply the rule again and square
steps.margin_note: Second mark. (m + n)(m − n) = m² − n² is what sits under the root, and the factor 2 cancels from top and bottom.
steps.memory_tip: (m + n) + (m − n) = 2m, and the cross term contains √(m² − n²).

lines.text: ∴ a : b = m + √(m² − n²) : m − √(m² − n²)

recall.must_convey: That squaring gives 2m ± 2√(m² − n²), and the 2 cancels to leave the required ratio.
accept: apply the rule a second time then square
m plus n plus m minus n is two m
the cross term is two root m squared minus n squared
square cheste two m plus two root m square minus n square
the two cancels from numerator and denominator

steps.why: Squaring adds the two brackets to 2m and leaves the cross term 2√((m + n)(m − n)) = 2√(m² − n²). The common factor 2 then cancels.
common_mistakes: Writing the cross term as 2√(m + n) + 2√(m − n) instead of one root of the product.
Replacing √(m² − n²) with m − n, which is not equal to it.
